previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of chronic pain, asplenia, recurrent venous thromboembolism, and long-term anticoagulation presented with pleuritic chest pain, fever, chills, and abdominal pain. He reported adherence to Lovenox and recent exposure to a family member with pneumonia. Initial evaluation revealed mild leukocytosis and stable vital signs. A prior CT angiogram from an outside hospital ruled out pulmonary embolism, and a repeat CT of the abdomen and pelvis showed no acute findings, though a stable nonocclusive thrombus near the IVC filter was noted. Empiric antibiotics were started due to concern for infection but were discontinued as symptoms resolved. Hemoptysis was minimal and consistent with chronic anticoagulation. The patient improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on his prior medications with instructions to follow up with primary care and hematology for monitoring of a stable lung nodule and kidney cyst.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male with hx. chronic pain, recurrent venous and 
arterial thromboses s/p IVC filter and on chronic lovenox 
presenting with chest pain and findings concerning for new 
aortic arch thrombus

# Aortic arch thrombus:  Patient has history of recurrent aortic 
and venous thromboses.  He has been seen in the past by the 
___ clinic at ___ but did not keep several follow-up 
appointments and was since lost to follow-up.   CT-A on ___ 
showed a thrombus on the proximal descending which was not 
apparent on repeat CT-A done ___.  CT-A done this 
admission incidentally revealed what appears to be a recurrence 
of this aortic arch thrombus.  Vascular surgery was consulted 
and felt the clot was in too delicate an area to warrant 
surgical intervention.  Hematology was consulted and recommended 
starting a heparin drip.  Etiology of patient's recurrence was 
unclear, as he claimed to be taking his lovenox as directed.  An 
anti fXa level was noted to subtherapeutic in the ED but this 
was likely drawn outside the 6h window from his most recent 
dose.  As per hematology, the patient was started on a full dose 
aspirin and his home lovenox dose.  A repeat anti-Xa level was 
drawn within 4 hours of his second dose of lovenox and was found 
to be therapeutic.  The patient is being discharged on his home 
lovenox dose in addition to aspirin.  He has close hematology 
follow-up to determine the etiology of his hypercoagulability 
(has had negative factor X leiden, negative anticardiolipin 
antibodies in the past) and for further recommendations for 
anticoagulation.  His simvastatin was increased to 40 mg daily 
for to further optimization of his clotting risk.

# Chronic pain: patient has a history of pain-med seeking.  He 
was terminated from his narcotics contract at ___ for seeking 
narcotics from multiple providers.  He has presented several 
times over the last few months with c/o chest pain, found to be 
noncardiac in nature.  A medrec was conducted with his pharmacy 
andit showed that he has filled multiple percocet prescriptions 
from no single provider over last several months.  His most 
recent prescription for oxycodone was 10 mg Q6H filled in mid 
___.  He was continued on this regimen while in house.

CHRONIC ISSUES
# HTN: continued HCTZ.
# Anxiety: continued ativan at night PRN
# Insomnia: continued home trazadone, also ativan at night 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
1.  Patient needs further workup re: hypercoagulability (factor 
V leiden and anticardiolipin negative in our system).
2.  Patient needs further management of his chronic pain and 
anxiety and consideration of interventions to reduce his 
dependence on narcotics.
3.  Vascular surgery has recommended repeat CT-A in 1 month to 
assess progress of clot.
4.  Patient was incidentally found to have intermediate left 
lower pole renal lesion with recommended ultrasound to confirm 
benignity.
